chunks: My father narrated to us, may Allah be pleased with him, with this chain, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him: Was Allah, Glorious and Exalted is He, consciously knowing of Himself before He created the creation? He, peace be upon him, said: Yes. I said: Was He seeing and hearing it? He said: He was not in need of that, because He was not asking it, nor requesting from it. He is His Self, and His Self is Him; His Might is Piercing, and so He does not need to name Himself. However, He indeed chose names for Himself, to others than Himself, that they may call upon Him with, because if He was not called upon by His Name, he would not have been recognized. Hence, the first He chose for Himself is the High, the Great, because He is the Highest of all things. So, His meaning is the God, and His Name is the High, the Great, which is the first of His Names, because He has exalted above everything.
ai.seo_question: What is the relationship between Allah's self-knowledge and His choice of names for creation?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Mani al-Akhbar*, Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) elucidates the doctrine of Allah's eternal self-knowledge, distinguishing between His intrinsic essence and the relational names chosen for creation's benefit. He identifies 'Al-Ali Al-Azim' as the primary name, reflecting His absolute transcendence, a concept deeply rooted in Shia theological discussions on the distinction between the Divine Essence (Dhat) and Attributes (Sifat). This explanation underscores that divine names are not merely descriptive but serve as means for creatures to recognize and invoke the Creator, aligning with the Shia emphasis on Tawhid al-Asma wa al-Sifat.
